candidates.title: The Charger Has A Favorite Person
candidates.one_line_concept: Their shared evening can be tracked by one long charging cable that keeps migrating toward whoever is pretending they do not need attention.
suggested_slide_arc: Zuv reaches for the charger near the desk; only the cable tail is left.
Aachu is on the rug using it, but has placed his phone beside hers so it can charge too.
They keep moving closer to the outlet without admitting they are choosing the same corner.
Payoff: both phones abandoned at 4 percent while they sit together beside the plug.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Zuv half-kneeling beside the desk, holding the empty plug end like evidence; Aachu visible in the background on the rug with the cable crossing the floor.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Both sitting shoulder-near but not face-crowded beside one wall outlet, phones lying untouched, cable loosely looping between them.
candidates.visual_potential: Strong single prop, clean eyelines, low anatomy risk, readable phone-screen staging without tiny text.
failure_risks: Cable path could become visually messy if overdrawn.
Needs clear phone/charger silhouettes so the joke lands instantly.
Avoid making it look like a tech complaint instead of affection.

candidates.title: His Bookmark Is Always Her Stuff
candidates.one_line_concept: Zuv keeps marking his book with whatever tiny thing Aachu left nearby, and every bookmark accidentally becomes a portrait of her.
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu notices her hair clip sticking out of Zuv's book.
Next slide: a receipt from their snack run used as a bookmark.
Next slide: a pressed tissue with her lipstick stain tucked between pages.
Payoff: Zuv opens the book and finds Aachu has placed a proper bookmark inside that says nothing, just a tiny drawn arrow pointing to her.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu standing beside a chair, pointing at her hair clip peeking from Zuv's open book on the armrest; Zuv caught mid-page-turn.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Close but not cramped tabletop frame: book open, handmade blank bookmark, Aachu's hand entering from one side, Zuv smiling down at the page.
candidates.visual_potential: Excellent prop sequence, intimate without face crowding, easy repeated object motif.
failure_risks: Lipstick/tissue detail must not become microtext or gross.
The payoff bookmark needs a simple visual symbol, not readable writing.
Must avoid making Zuv look careless with her things.

candidates.title: The Snack Bowl Treaty
candidates.one_line_concept: They silently negotiate love through how many chips each leaves in the bowl, until the last one becomes a ceremony.
suggested_slide_arc: Both hands reach into the bowl at the same time and freeze.
Aachu pushes the bowl slightly toward Zuv while looking away.
Zuv pushes it back with one remaining chip arranged in the center.
Payoff: the last chip is broken in half with absurd seriousness.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Top-down-ish table scene: two hands hovering over a bowl, two faces visible above the table edge, both pretending not to notice.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: A clean lower-frame close scene of the chip split on a napkin, their two hands each holding half, faces softly in upper space.
candidates.visual_potential: Very shareable couple behavior, tactile, low-risk, phone-readable, with natural baked-in text space above.
failure_risks: Could become generic if the hands are the only emotional proof.
Needs precise eyeline comedy, not just cute sharing.

candidates.title: The Door He Holds For Her Mood
candidates.one_line_concept: Zuv does not just hold the door; he keeps holding the exact emotional pause Aachu needs before entering the day.
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu stands just inside the doorway with one shoe on, not ready yet.
Zuv is outside holding the door open, looking back without rushing her.
She picks up one forgotten thing, then another, while he shifts the door from hand to elbow.
Payoff: he is still there, now holding the door, her keys, and one tiny plant she decided had to come too.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Interior threshold composition: Aachu framed by the doorway putting on one shoe; Zuv outside in profile holding the door, bright negative space above.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Zuv at the open door with keys and small plant pot balanced safely, Aachu stepping out calmer, both faces separated enough to preserve identity.
candidates.visual_potential: Fresh care without stereotype if staged as patience, not rescue; strong threshold metaphor and prop accumulation.
failure_risks: Can drift into generic care if the objects are not specific and funny.
Avoid too many props in the payoff.

candidates.title: She Saves The Best Light For Him
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu keeps adjusting the room so Zuv lands in the nicest patch of evening light without realizing she has made him the scene.
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu opens the curtain a little while Zuv reads on the sofa.
She moves a mug, then a cushion, then the lamp, all to keep the warm patch on him.
Zuv finally notices the whole room has been quietly rearranged around his chair.
Payoff: he shifts over and leaves half the light for her.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu by the curtain pulling it open with one hand; Zuv seated in a clean sun patch, unaware, book or notebook in lap.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Two separate readable faces in one sofa composition, sitting in the shared rectangle of light, props slightly rearranged around them.
candidates.visual_potential: Beautiful house-style fit, airy negative space, emotional without crowding, but needs action beats so it does not become only mood.
failure_risks: Light may become too atmospheric unless props prove the joke.
Could feel less instantly shareable than stronger everyday-behavior ideas.
Must avoid yellow parchment cast while showing warm light.

candidates.title: The Remote Control Custody Battle
candidates.one_line_concept: The remote keeps changing hands, but the real joke is that neither of them is actually watching anymore.
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu points the remote at the TV with full seriousness.
Zuv slides a bowl or cushion across the table as a peace offering for the remote.
The remote sits exactly between them like a tiny courtroom exhibit.
Payoff: the TV is still on the menu screen while they are laughing at each other instead.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu on one side of the sofa holding the remote upright; Zuv on the other side offering a snack bowl, TV glow implied but not dominant.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Wide sofa scene with the remote abandoned in the center cushion, both looking at each other, TV menu barely visible as background proof.
candidates.visual_potential: Very readable prop comedy, strong share/save behavior, easy carousel rhythm.
failure_risks: TV screen must not require readable microtext.
Could become sitcom-generic unless the handoff rituals feel intimate.
Keep faces apart; avoid tangled sofa pose.

top_pick.title: The Charger Has A Favorite Person
top_pick.reason: It has the cleanest visual proof: one cable tells the whole relationship without needing microtext, face crowding, or generic care.

visual_risks: Avoid tiny screen text, receipts, or labels.
Keep faces separated enough for reference-driven identity.
Use props as proof, not clutter.
Do not let care beats become one-sided service.
Warm light must not become yellow parchment.
